page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.16-256 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance within the Standard series. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB allocation per virtual core to accommodate memory-intensive operations.

Hardware accelerators are not present on this machine, with a GPU count of zero. Local NVMe storage is omitted from the hardware configuration, meaning all persistence requires the provisioning of network-attached block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned for external network accessibility. The balance of 32 dedicated compute threads against 256.0 GB of memory provides substantial operational headroom for non-accelerated computing tasks that exceed typical memory allocations.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration serves environments where RAM capacity dictates system scale. It is suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) batch processing, and memory-constrained enterprise application servers.
